text:
[NLFC.8.3] **A clone starts with no callbacks registered.** `ds_engine_clone`
**must** return the clone with every callback empty and no `user` pointer
copied: the stream, call, log and metric callbacks and both cache
hooks. The integrator registers what the
clone needs before pumping it, as on a new engine. An essential verb with no
handler registered fails the clone's pump as it would a new engine's
(`DS_ERR_STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE`, [NERR.7]). So until the integrator wires it,
nothing a clone does reaches the source's host state.

For the shadow-engine speculate / commit / discard use case, the integrator
registers effect-buffering wrappers on the clone before pumping it. The
reads-live / writes-buffered split and the single-pump scope limit are an
integrator-guide how-to, not part of this contract.
